title: Emissions & EVAP Diagnostics
summary: Compact emissions and EVAP hub for check engine light, fuel smell, small and large EVAP leaks, purge faults, vent faults, and smoke-test workflows.
intro: Use this hub when an emissions fault needs to be separated into cap, hose, purge, vent, canister, wiring, or smoke-test evidence before pricing parts.

common_symptoms.description: Use when fuel odor, rich running, or raw-fuel clues overlap with emissions or catalyst risk.

common_symptoms.title: Poor Fuel Economy
common_symptoms.description: Use when emissions faults come with fuel-trim, oxygen sensor, or rich-running evidence.

common_symptoms.title: Rough Idle

diagnostic_path_sections.title: EVAP Leak and Smoke-Test Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Start here for P0442, P0455, fuel smell near the vehicle, or failed EVAP monitor complaints.
checks: Inspect fuel cap seal, filler neck, visible EVAP hoses, and canister connections
Smoke test the EVAP system when the leak is not obvious
Confirm the leak location before pricing purge, vent, hose, cap, or canister work
confidence_cues: Small leaks need careful sealing checks

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Purge and Idle Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when purge flow faults, rough idle, fuel smell, or vacuum-style symptoms overlap.
checks: Command or isolate the purge valve and check whether it seals when closed
Compare fuel trims at idle and cruise before blaming the oxygen sensor
Inspect purge hoses and wiring when circuit or flow codes are present
confidence_cues: Fuel trims help separate leak type

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Vent and Canister Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when the tank will not vent, filling is difficult, or vent-control codes return after leak checks.
checks: Command the vent valve and confirm it opens, closes, and seals
Inspect vent filter, canister contamination, dirt intrusion, and underbody corrosion
Check circuit power, ground, and connector condition before replacing the valve
confidence_cues: Canister contamination can change the estimate

inspection_priority: Confirm the exact EVAP code family and freeze-frame context first.
Inspect cap, filler neck, hoses, purge, vent, and canister connections before replacing valves.
Use smoke testing when the leak source is not visible or when the code returns after simple checks.
confidence_cues: Leak size changes the test plan
Purge and vent faults need different checks
Fuel smell should not be treated as one automatic part
estimate_guidance: Use EVAP diagnosis or smoke testing when the leak source has not been proven.
Move to purge or vent valve replacement only when command, sealing, flow, or circuit checks support that side.
Keep catalyst or oxygen-sensor pricing separate from EVAP leak repair unless scan data connects the systems.
